anchors.interpretation: Medicare-relative prices can anchor scenarios for efficient delivery, but a blanket 100 percent target is not admissible because aggregate margins, hospital heterogeneity, rural/safety-net needs, quality, and access differ.
The Medicare fee schedule is a same-service reference, but specialty mix, geographic input costs, safety-net service, misvalued relative rates, and future access require explicit floors.

admissibility_rules: Use service-level rather than provider-wide averages.
Adjust for geography, wages, teaching, uncompensated care, case mix, and safety-net role.
Test rural, critical-access, and low-volume providers separately.
Preserve beneficiary access, wait time, network adequacy, and clinician participation.
Preserve or improve risk-adjusted mortality, readmission, patient experience, and appropriate utilization.
Phase and monitor any scenario; stop or revise when an access or quality floor fails.
next_gate: Construct low, central, and high Medicare-relative scenarios by service and provider class, then test each against access, quality, and adequacy floors before estimating gross or net fiscal effects.
